title: CMAs with Craig - April 1, 2026
summary: Hands-on CMA training session where Craig walks agents through real-world property pricing scenarios. Covers duplex valuation using sales comparables vs gross rent multiplier, COVID-era purchase pricing traps, builder MLS manipulation tactics, floor plan and location defects that affect value, commission negotiation scripts, and how to handle unrealistic seller expectations.

broker_guidance.scenario: Pricing a duplex or multi-unit property
broker_guidance.guidance: When comps are plentiful and similar, use sales comparable method instead of gross rent multiplier. Verify zoning with the city. Check tax records for actual square footage and building count. For side-by-side duplexes, they typically command slightly more than up-and-down units. Adjust for garages, carports, and condition.
broker_guidance.client_language: Based on the comparable sales in your immediate neighborhood, similar side-by-side duplexes are trading in the upper five hundreds to low six hundreds.

broker_guidance.scenario: Seller wants to price based on COVID-era purchase
broker_guidance.guidance: COVID peak purchases (Oct 2021) are a trap. The market dropped after those peaks before recovering. Show sellers that their purchase price may have been at the absolute top, and current comps likely don't support gains. Be direct about potential losses.
broker_guidance.client_language: You bought at the absolute peak of the market. The data shows homes in your neighborhood are trading in the 1.0 to 1.2 range. Your home has additional floor plan and location issues that push you toward the lower end.

broker_guidance.scenario: Floor plan or location defects affecting value
broker_guidance.guidance: Floor plan problems (steep driveway, garage on lower level, hiking groceries up stairs) and location defects (busy roads, intersections) are real value killers. Craig discounts busy roads 5% or more. Don't let sellers compare to homes without these issues.
broker_guidance.client_language: Every buyer who sees this home will note the driveway and floor plan issue. People are willing to spend more for a smaller home that doesn't have this problem.

broker_guidance.guidance: Some builders are listing sold transactions as 'canceled' to hide price drops from appraisers and future buyers. They negotiate off-MLS deals with buyer agents. This creates artificial scarcity and inflated appraisal support. Be aware when pulling comps in new construction areas.
broker_guidance.client_language: The builder is trying to protect their inventory by not reporting the actual sale price. This is why we need to look at real closed data, not just MLS status.

broker_guidance.guidance: When sellers use AI tools or their own analysis with no comps, suggest a desktop or full appraisal as a reality check. If they still won't listen, consider cancellation penalties or walking away. Don't waste time and marketing dollars on guaranteed failures.
broker_guidance.client_language: If the data doesn't support the price, no amount of marketing will sell it. An independent appraisal might help set realistic expectations.

broker_guidance.guidance: Never defend your commission upfront. Ask: 'What's been your experience with selling homes and commissions?' Let them talk themselves into valuing quality. Ask what other agents quoted. If they're between 2-3%, you're in range. Offer performance-based tiers: full commission if you hit the target, reduced if you have to drop price significantly.
broker_guidance.client_language: What was your experience with that one percent agent? ... So if I'm between two and three percent, then I would be someone you'd consider, correct?

broker_guidance.scenario: Verifying square footage and property details
broker_guidance.guidance: Always cross-check MLS square footage against county tax records. If a listing says 'from county records' but the numbers don't match, that's a red flag. For multi-unit properties, verify each building's square footage and whether it's legally a duplex through parcel maps and zoning.
broker_guidance.client_language: The tax records show 5,000 square feet, not 5,400. And the remark says it was taken from county records, but it wasn't. That's a problem we need to address.

broker_guidance.guidance: Seller financing deals often sell above market value because unsophisticated investors overpay for easy terms. Look for clues: short days on market, quick close, terms mentioned in remarks. These comps may need to be excluded or heavily adjusted.
broker_guidance.client_language: This one sold at $700K when everything else is in the low sixes. The remarks mention seller financing at 5% with 10% down. That's likely an inflated price due to financing terms, not true market value.

steps: Verify property details against county tax records before starting CMA
Check parcel maps and zoning for multi-unit properties
Use sales comparable method when similar comps exist nearby
Use gross rent multiplier or cap rate only when comps are scarce
Adjust for floor plan defects, location issues, and condition differences
Discount busy roads and intersections by 5% or more
Exclude or adjust seller financing comps that inflate prices
Watch for builder manipulation of MLS status and sold data
Handle commission discussions by asking about past experiences first
Suggest appraisals for unrealistic sellers who won't accept data
Set cancellation penalties for unmotivated sellers testing the market

objections.objection: Seller says their home is worth more because of upgrades
objections.response: Upgrades don't always equal value. Compare to similarly upgraded homes in the same neighborhood. If their 'upgrades' are standard for the area, there's no premium. AI tools often overvalue upgrades.

objections.objection: Seller wants to use COVID-era purchase as baseline
objections.response: COVID peak prices dropped before recovering. Show them the actual trajectory: peak, drop, partial recovery. Their purchase may have been at the top, and current values may be lower than they paid.

objections.objection: Seller compares to homes in better locations
objections.response: You can't compare to homes on flat lots with no busy roads. Location defects are real value killers. Show them the actual comps in their immediate area with similar issues.

objections.objection: Builder claims homes are selling at list price
objections.response: Builders may be hiding actual sale prices by marking them canceled or negotiating concessions off-MLS. Ask for the real net price, not the advertised number.

objections.objection: Seller wants a discount commission without discounting price
objections.response: Commission directly affects marketing budget and effort. If they want full service, they need to pay for it. Offer performance-based pricing instead of flat discounts.
